AR-2026F-HB1007.s: This act would set funding for the Arkansas Department of Education’s public school fund for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It would provide money for local school districts, special programs, school employee insurance, teacher pay, student support, technology, and other school aid. The total amount appropriated is $3,662,266,811, and it also sets funding and staff limits for the public school computer network and education renewal zones.

AR-2026F-HB1009.s: Act 118 sets the state budget for the Department of Public Safety for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027. It covers pay and expenses for shared services, crime victims reparations, public safety equipment grants, and federal operations. The act includes $5 million for the Public Safety Equipment Grant Program and other set amounts for these programs.

AR-2026F-HB1010.s: This act gives money for the Arkansas Department of Corrections, Division of Community Correction, for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It sets funds for salaries and operations, including $78,249,356 for state operations, $14,862,870 for special revenue operations, and $75,000 for federal asset forfeiture. It also lets the division hire up to 912 regular employees and 10 temporary or part-time workers, and it took effect on July 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-HB1011.s: Now Act 120, it sets money and staff limits for the Arkansas Department of Corrections for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It provides funds for shared services, county jail reimbursements to counties that house state inmates, and sex offender assessment work. The act also sets the highest number of regular jobs for the division and lists pay limits for those jobs.

AR-2026F-HB1017.s: This act sets spending for the Arkansas Department of Agriculture’s promotion boards for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027. It gives money for the beef, catfish, corn and grain sorghum, rice, soybean, and wheat boards, with set amounts for operations, research, and related work. It also lets the state fiscal officer waive some fund deductions for certain agriculture fees from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, and the act takes effect on July 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-HB1018.s: Act 122 makes money available for the University of Arkansas East Arkansas Community College for fiscal year 2026-2027. It sets pay limits and staffing levels for regular jobs and temporary help, and it sets aside funds for salaries, extra help, staff matching costs, operating expenses, and travel. The act includes $6,489,324 for regular salaries, $175,000 for extra help, $2,125,000 for matching costs, $2,588,321 for operating expenses, and $60,000 for conference and travel.

AR-2026F-HB1020.s: This act sets funding for the Arkansas Department of Transportation for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It sets pay and job limits for department staff and covers personal services and operating costs.

AR-2026F-HB1022.s: The bill would give the Arkansas Development Finance Authority money for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It sets aside $15,000,000 for the Federal Housing Program and $2,296,487 for grants and aid tied to emergency shelters and help for homeless people and families. It also sets pay rules for agency jobs and allows up to 20 extra positions if growth needs come up. The act would take effect on July 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-HB1023.s: This measure makes funding for the Arkansas Department of Human Services Secretary’s Office for fiscal year 2026-2027. It sets money for staff pay, extra help, office costs, data services, and building work, including $69,893,961 for operations and $15,914,729 for construction. It also sets the largest number of regular jobs and temporary help the office may use. The bill passed the legislature and was sent to the governor.

AR-2026F-HB1024.s: The act gives money for the Arkansas Department of Parks, Heritage, and Tourism, Division of Heritage, for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It sets staff limits and funding for shared services, state operations, conservation tax work, and the Delta Cultural Center. It also sets money for pay, extra help, travel, grants, building work, and other operating costs.

AR-2026F-HB1034.s: The bill would fund the Arkansas Office of the Treasurer of State for fiscal year 2026-2027. It sets pay and staffing limits, including up to 33 regular employees and 5 temporary or part-time workers, and sets aside $7,974,734 for salaries, operations, data services, and related programs. It would take effect on July 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-HB1035.s: The bill would fund the Arkansas Department of Health’s tobacco prevention and cessation programs for fiscal year 2026-2027. It sets staff limits, including 31 regular employees and up to 4 temporary workers, and gives the program $14,702,255. It also lets the department move $500,000 from the prevention and cessation account to the Breast Cancer Control Fund for the state match on breast and cervical cancer services. The emergency clause was adopted, and the act would take effect on July 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-HB1036.s: The bill would set the Department of Health’s budget for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It sets pay and job limits for staff and sets aside money for personal services and operating costs, including $425,501 for Shared Services. It also sets the maximum number of employees for several parts of the department, including 2,203 for Operations.

AR-2026F-HB1041.s: Act 125 sets the 2026-2027 budget for the Arkansas Secretary of State. It covers salaries, office and election costs, Capitol Police expenses, building and grounds work, refunds, voting system grants, and other set programs. The act includes a $11,000,000 county voting system grant and takes effect for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027.

AR-2026F-HB1053.s: The bill would set spending for personal services and operating costs for the University of Arkansas at Little Rock for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027. It also sets the highest number of workers and pay limits for many campus jobs. The measure has passed the House and Senate and includes an emergency clause.

AR-2026F-HB1055.s: Act 126 sets the state budget for the Department of Education’s Office of Early Childhood for fiscal year 2026-2027. It funds salaries, office costs, grants, and related work, including $14,635,808 for operations, $188,667,976 in federal money, $9,000,000 for child care program grants, and $200,000 for childcare facility grants. The act takes effect on July 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-HB1064.s: The bill would set aside money for the Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration to pay for a range of state programs in fiscal year 2026-2027. It includes funds for interstate groups, state pay items, grants, pension and relief funds, disaster aid, unemployment claims, and court cost refunds. It also sets money for child abuse and domestic violence services, justice programs, the Arkansas Sheriffs' Association, and drug enforcement and education.

AR-2026F-HB1066.s: This bill would set the 2026-2027 budget for the Department of Energy and Environment’s Division of Environmental Quality. It sets pay and spending limits for shared services, state operations, federal operations, and the wastewater licensing program, including a $16,834,853 federal operations amount and a $320,927 wastewater licensing amount. It also sets staff limits for the division, including up to 347 regular employees and 70 temporary or part-time workers.

AR-2026F-HB1077.s: The act sets spending and staffing limits for the Arkansas Department of Human Services, Division of County Operations, for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It includes money for salaries, operations, grants, Medicaid tobacco settlement work, emergency rental help, and Summer EBT, along with up to 2,010 regular employees and 43 extra-help workers. It also requires a yearly $7.5 million transfer from TANF funds to the Arkansas Better Chance Program and directs the department to seek a federal waiver to limit what TANF cash assistance can buy.

AR-2026F-HB1100.s: Now Act 143, the law changes Arkansas rules for how state general revenue is split among many funds and fund accounts starting July 1, 2026. It also creates funds and lets money be moved to and from funds and fund accounts. The act sets monthly allocation limits for schools, state agencies, counties, colleges, and other public programs.

AR-2026F-HCMR1001.s: The Arkansas legislature passed a memorial resolution honoring Bishop Kenneth Lydell Robinson Sr. and recognizing his work in the state and his local community. It says he was a pastor, singer, musician, radio host, businessman, and church leader in Central Arkansas. A copy of the resolution would be given to his wife and family.

AR-2026F-HR1013.s: The resolution would authorize a bill to change Arkansas rules for digital asset mining businesses and businesses using blockchain networks. It would also change what local governments can do about these businesses, including home digital asset mining. The bill text would update the Arkansas Data Centers Act of 2023 and related local rules.

AR-2026F-HR1014.s: The measure would let lawmakers introduce a bill that would require digital asset miners and related businesses to give written notice before buying or leasing land or a building, or before starting construction for a mining site. The notice would go to the Arkansas Public Service Commission and the local government at least six months ahead of time.

AR-2026F-HR1015.s: The resolution would allow a bill to be introduced that changes the rules for industrial development authorities in Arkansas. It would update who can serve on their boards, allow removal for good cause, say they must follow local planning and zoning rules, and change how they can use eminent domain, which is the power to take property for public use with payment.

AR-2026F-HR1016.s: This resolution would let a bill be introduced to create a state law about certain residential property deals owned by business entities. The bill would require clear disclosure that a buyer is buying an interest in the entity, not the home itself, and it would limit certain rules on transfers, fees, and dispute forums. It would also give the Attorney General enforcement power and set some exceptions for certain religious and nonprofit property and for time-share interests.

AR-2026F-HR1020.s: The House adopted a resolution honoring Frederick Henry Middleton for his 50 years of service to the City of Arkadelphia. It thanks him for his work and wishes him well in retirement. A copy of the resolution would be given to him by the House Chief Clerk.

AR-2026F-HR1021.s: The House would designate May 2026 as Skin Cancer Awareness Month. It would also encourage Arkansans to learn more about skin cancer risks and the need for early diagnosis. Copies of the resolution would be sent to several Arkansas medical groups and the University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences medical school and dermatology department.

AR-2026F-HR1022.s: This resolution would congratulate the Rollin' Razorbacks of Sherwood for winning the Division II national wheelchair basketball championship. It says the team won its sixth national title and beat the Memorial Rehabilitation Sharks 61-51 on March 29, 2026. A copy of the resolution would be given to head coach Jared Johnson.

AR-2026F-HR1028.s: This resolution would recognize the Rogers High School Lady Mounties girls' cross country team as the 2024 6A State Champions. It also says a copy would be given to Head Coach Powell Bryant after adoption. The resolution names the team members and coaches and describes their 2024 season.

AR-2026F-HR1029.s: The House resolution recognizes the Rogers High School Mounties baseball team as the 2025 Class 6A state champions. It notes the team won the title game 7-6, finished the season 27-4, and lists several players and coaches. The resolution was adopted and a copy is to be given to Head Coach Brian Fowler.

AR-2026F-HR1030.s: This House resolution recognizes the Rogers High School Mounties boys' tennis team for winning the 2024 Class 6A State Tennis Tournament. It also notes the team’s 11-1 season, the players and coach, and some of their honors. The House adopted the resolution, and a copy would be given to Head Coach Matt Fulton.

AR-2026F-HR1031.s: The resolution would recognize the Rogers High School Lady Mounties girls' wrestling team as the 2026 Class 6A state champions. It also says a copy of the resolution would be given to Coach Willie Wright. The team won the title on February 14, 2026, and the resolution lists the team and coaches by name.

AR-2026F-HR1032.s: The Arkansas House resolution would recognize the Rogers High School Mounties boys golf team as the 2025 Class 6A state champions. It also says a copy of the resolution would be given to Coach Marcus Alexander.

AR-2026F-HR1038.s: The House adopted a resolution recognizing April as Child Abuse Prevention Month in Arkansas. It also commends the Court Appointed Special Advocate, or CASA, programs and their staff and volunteers. A copy of the resolution would be sent to Arkansas CASA programs.

AR-2026F-HR1040.s: This resolution would recognize the Mountain Home High School Bombers boys' cross country team as the 2025 Class 5A state champions. It says the team won the title in Hot Springs on November 7, 2025, and notes that some team members earned All-State honors. A copy of the resolution would be given to Head Coach Wil Norris.

AR-2026F-HR1041.s: This resolution would formally recognize the Mountain Home High School girls' cross country team as the 2025 Class 5A state champions. It notes that the team won the title on November 7, 2025, and that three runners earned All-State honors. A copy of the resolution would be given to Head Coach Tilda Helgesson.

AR-2026F-HR1042.s: A House resolution would recognize the Mansfield High School Lady Tigers volleyball team as the 2025 Class 3A state champions. It notes the team won the title on November 1, 2025, by beating Harding Academy 3-1. A copy of the resolution would be given to Head Coach Kaylie Pyles.

AR-2026F-HR1043.s: The Arkansas House resolution would recognize the North Little Rock High School Lady Charging Wildcats girls' basketball team as the 2026 Class 6A state champions. It says the team won the title on March 14, 2026, and that a copy of the resolution would be given to the coaching staff.

AR-2026F-HR1044.s: The House resolution recognizes the Mount Saint Mary Academy Belles golf team as the 2025 Class 6A state champions. It says the team won the state title in Rogers and notes members of the team and their coach. The resolution was adopted, and a copy is to be given to Head Coach Laura Freville.

AR-2026F-HR1045.s: This resolution would congratulate the Central Arkansas Christian High School Choir for its awards at the 2026 State Choral Festival. It notes the choir won Best in Class 3A Medium Mixed Chorus and Best in Class 3A Overall Medium Chorus, and says a copy would be given to the choir director.

AR-2026F-HR1047.s: This house resolution would recognize Coach Dave Wilbers for his work with the Arkansas Tech University Golden Suns women’s basketball team and congratulate him on his retirement. It also says a copy of the resolution would be given to him by the House chief clerk. The resolution lists his team’s wins, titles, and tournament appearances during his 19 seasons as head coach.

AR-2026F-HR1048.s: The Arkansas House would honor the Arkansas Tech University Golden Suns women's cross country team for winning the Great American Conference Championship. It would also note that Coach Gabe Sams would receive a copy of the resolution. The resolution names several team members and coaches and says the team won its first conference title.

AR-2026F-HR1049.s: The House would adopt a resolution recognizing Kopper Kettle Candies for its candy-making work and for being named the top candy store in Arkansas and the fifth best in the United States. A copy of the resolution would be given to Thomas Greer by the House chief clerk.

AR-2026F-HR1050.s: This resolution would recognize the Joe T. Robinson High School Senators football team as the 2025 Class 5A state champions. It says the team won the title game 34-19 and finished the season 14-0. A copy of the resolution would be given to Head Coach Tyler Uptergrove.

AR-2026F-HR1051.s: The House resolution would recognize the Joe T. Robinson High School boys' swim and dive team as the 2026 Class 1A-4A state champions. It also says a copy of the resolution would be given to coaches Jackie Bracey and Srdan Markovic. The team won the state meet on February 28, 2026, and several team members set or matched state marks.

AR-2026F-HR1052.s: This resolution would take away Arkansas Girls State’s access to the House chamber for its 2026 meeting and would bar it from using bill drafting help from the Bureau of Legislative Research. If the Speaker later decides the students who were denied a chance to participate have been allowed to join the 2026 meeting, the change would be undone and the access restored. It also urges the American Legion Auxiliary to reconsider any decision that would block those students from taking part.

AR-2026F-SB10.s: The measure sets state spending for the Arkansas Department of Commerce, Division of Workforce Services, for fiscal year 2026-2027. It covers salaries, office costs, unemployment benefit payments, training help, grants, and other work of the division. The bill includes several funding pots, including $16,258,332 for operations, $63,610,021 from the trust fund, and $702,000,001 for unemployment benefits and related expenses.

AR-2026F-SB13.s: The law gives money for the Arkansas Judicial Discipline and Disability Commission for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It sets funds for staff pay, office costs, travel, professional fees, and investigator expenses, for a total of $804,239. It took effect on July 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-SB15.s: This bill would set aside money for the Arkansas Department of Parks, Heritage, and Tourism for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It covers state park and tourism work, including salaries, extra help, grants, advertising, and conservation tax operations. The bill also sets staff limits for those programs.

AR-2026F-SB16.s: Now law, it sets the 2026-2027 budget for the Capitol Zoning District Commission in the Department of Parks, Heritage, and Tourism. It allows up to 3 regular employees and 1 temporary worker. It sets aside $257,040 for salaries and operating costs, plus $2,000 from a cash fund for operating expenses. It takes effect on July 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-SB20.s: Act 132 makes state money available for the Arkansas Department of Human Services, Division of Medical Services, for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It sets funds for staff pay and operating costs, Medicaid grant payments, nursing home closure costs, receivership expenses, and nursing home quality grants. It also sets rules for how Medicaid rates are calculated and lets the division change rates in some cases, with some changes needing approval from lawmakers.

AR-2026F-SB21.s: This bill would set the budget for the Arkansas Department of Human Services division that handles aging, adult, and behavioral health services for fiscal year 2026-2027. It would allow money for staff, operating costs, grants, aging and adult services, community alcohol safety grants, patient benefits, and mental health grants. It also sets the maximum number of regular and temporary workers for the division.

AR-2026F-SB23.s: The measure became law as Act 133 and sets spending for the Arkansas Department of Human Services' Division of Youth Services for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It provides money for staff, operations, community sanctions, community services, federal child and youth service grants, and residential services, including a total of $14,533,752 for operations and $34,616,356 for residential services. It also allows up to $240,000 for the Juvenile Ombudsman Program and $400,000 for local juvenile detention facilities.

AR-2026F-SB3.s: The bill would set spending and staff limits for the Arkansas Department of Shared Administrative Services for fiscal year 2026-2027. It covers pay and operations for statewide shared services, marketing and redistribution, the purchase and corporate travel card program, information technology, commission stipends and mileage, and the employee benefits division. The bill also sets aside specific amounts, including $15,589,911 for statewide shared services operations and $4,000,000 for refunds and reimbursements in the travel card program.

AR-2026F-SB30.s: This act became law and sets the Governor’s Office budget for fiscal year 2026-2027. It covers pay and operating costs, with $6,493,405 for operations and $500,000 for the governor’s emergency proclamation fund. It also sets the office’s staff and temporary worker limits for that year, and it takes effect on July 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-SB31.s: This bill would fund the Arkansas Administrative Office of the Courts for fiscal year 2026-2027. It sets staff levels and pays for court operations, interpreter services, judicial education, dispute resolution, hearing and vision aids for jurors, district judge training, and dependency-neglect representation. The bill sets out a total of several appropriations for these programs, including $7,216,024 for operations and $8,669,335 for dependency-neglect representation.

AR-2026F-SB36.s: Creates the state budget for the Arkansas Department of Agriculture for fiscal year 2026-2027. It sets staff limits and funding for shared services and operations, including money for salaries, extra help, travel, fees, and other operating costs. The bill became Act 135.

AR-2026F-SB39.s: This law sets state funding rules for Arkansas State University for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It sets the maximum number of employees and salary levels for many university jobs. The law affects Arkansas State University and its campuses and units.

AR-2026F-SB4.s: The bill sets money and staff limits for several Arkansas Department of Health licensing and regulation boards for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It covers boards such as acupuncture, alcoholism and drug abuse counseling, athletic training, chiropractic examiners, counseling, dental examiners, and dietetics. The funds would pay for salaries, office costs, travel, and other operating expenses for those boards.

AR-2026F-SB43.s: This act sets the budget for the University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture for fiscal year 2026-2027. It covers regular salaries, part-time or temporary help, and operating costs for the division. The law sets the regular salary line at $53,527,071 for state operations.

AR-2026F-SB5.s: Now law, this act gives the Arkansas Tobacco Settlement Commission money for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It sets aside $357,456 for salaries, benefits, office costs, travel, and professional fees, and it allows one regular employee position. The money is for monitoring program spending and for grants, with the act taking effect July 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-SB55.s: The act sets spending for the Arkansas Supreme Court and the Supreme Court Bar of Arkansas for fiscal year 2026-2027. It funds salaries, extra help, and operating costs, including $7,666,202 for court operations and $5,733,581 for the Bar of Arkansas. It also sets the maximum number of staff for each office and takes effect on July 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-SB56.s: The measure became Act 68 and sets aside money for continuing education and certification programs for county clerks, circuit clerks, county treasurers, county collectors, and county coroners in fiscal year 2026-2027. It provides $75,000 each for the county clerks, circuit clerks, county treasurers, and county collectors programs, and $125,000 for the county coroners program. The act takes effect on July 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-SB58.s: This law sets spending limits for the Arkansas Department of Education, Division of Higher Education for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It covers staff pay, office costs, grants, scholarships, technical education, research grants, and health education aid and loans. The bill sets aside amounts such as $71,550,000 for student grants and scholarships and $7,117,770 for health education grants and loans.

AR-2026F-SB63.s: This act gives the Department of Human Services $2 million for aging and adult services, including senior citizen centers. It also moves $2 million from the General Revenue Allotment Reserve Fund to pay for those costs. The law took effect right away when it was approved.

AR-2026F-SB67.s: This act gives the University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences $5 million for its High-Risk Pregnancy Program and IDHI Stroke Program. The money comes from the General Revenue Allotment Reserve Fund and is moved to the University of Arkansas Medical Center Fund. It took effect when it was signed into law on April 29, 2026.

AR-2026F-SB7.s: The bill would set spending limits for the Arkansas Department of Commerce’s State Insurance Department for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It covers money for staff pay, office costs, fraud investigations, funeral services, prepaid funeral benefits, refunds of overpayments, continuing education, and health information counseling. The bill also sets the highest number of regular and temporary workers allowed for the department.

AR-2026F-SB73.s: This act adds $10 million for the Arkansas Economic Development Commission’s Community Assistance Grant Program. The money is for community assistance grants and is taken from the state’s General Revenue Allotment Reserve Fund. It became Act 141 and took effect when approved.

AR-2026F-SB75.s: Arkansas Act 144 changes the state revenue law and sets how state money is moved into many funds and fund accounts. It updates monthly transfer rules for the 2026-2027 fiscal year and after, including schools, health services, higher education, state agencies, counties, and cities. The act also declares an emergency, so it takes effect right away.

AR-2026F-SB76.s: This law gives $2 million for matching grants to county extension offices for capital improvements through the University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture. It is for the 2026-2027 fiscal year and is paid from state funds set by the chief fiscal officer. It took effect on July 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-SB77.s: This bill would set aside $550,000 for the Department of Education’s Educational Television Division to help pay annual Public Broadcasting Service membership dues for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. The state money would match private donations one for one, with payments tied to donations certified on two dates before the funds expire on June 30, 2027.

AR-2026F-SB8.s: Now law as Act 129, it sets the 2026-2027 budget for the Arkansas Department of Commerce and its economic development work. It funds salaries, office costs, grants, and business incentive programs, including money for community assistance, disaster recovery, the Arkansas Acceleration Fund, and super projects. The act also sets the most employees allowed in several department units for that year.

AR-2026F-SMR1.s: This Senate memorial resolution honors Senator Gary Don Stubblefield and recognizes his service to Arkansas and his local community. It says an official copy would be given to his wife and family after adoption. The resolution was adopted on April 14, 2026.

AR-2026F-SMR2.s: This Senate memorial resolution would honor former Senator Luther Boyd "Lu" Hardin and recognize his contributions to Arkansas and his local community. It notes his work in the state Senate, higher education, and university leadership. A copy of the resolution would be sent to his family after adoption.

AR-2026F-SMR3.s: This Senate memorial resolution remembers former Senator Uvalde Rex Lindsey and recognizes his work for Arkansas and his local community. It says a copy of the resolution would be given to his wife and family. The measure was adopted by the Senate.

AR-2026F-SMR4.s: The Senate would honor the memory of former Representative Stanley Jack “Stan” Berry and recognize his service to Arkansas and his local community. It notes his time in the National Guard, local boards and groups, and his service in the House of Representatives. If adopted, a copy would be given to his wife and family.

AR-2026F-SMR5.s: This Senate memorial resolution remembers attorney John Gill and recognizes his many contributions to Little Rock, Arkansas, and the practice of law in the state. It also says an appropriate copy should be given to his wife and family after adoption. The Senate adopted the resolution.

AR-2026F-SMR6.s: This memorial resolution would honor former University of Arkansas football coach Lou Holtz for his service to the university, the state, and the sport of football. It would also ask that a copy be given to his family if adopted.

AR-2026F-SR1.s: This resolution would have the Senate and House meet together on April 8, 2026, in the House Chamber to hear an address from Arkansas Governor Sarah Sanders. It was adopted by the Senate.

AR-2026F-SR10.s: The resolution would let a bill be introduced to change two Arkansas laws: the Arkansas Data Centers Act of 2023 and the Uniform Money Services Act. The proposed bill would remove a rule that keeps home digital asset mining and digital asset mining businesses from being treated as money transmitters, and it would add them to the law’s list of money transmission activities. People already doing that work in Arkansas would have to apply for a license by September 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-SR11.s: The resolution would let lawmakers introduce a bill that would require digital asset miners and digital asset mining businesses to give written notice before buying or leasing land or a building, or before starting construction. The notice would go to the Arkansas Public Service Commission and the local government where the work is planned. It would apply to projects for digital asset mining or for using a blockchain network.

AR-2026F-SR12.s: The resolution would let a senator introduce a bill about blockchain networks and digital asset mining, which are used to run some digital currencies. It would direct Arkansas state agencies to watch how these operations affect water use and the electric grid, and it would let them act if they threaten water supplies or grid reliability. It also sets a deadline for the first rules to be filed by January 1, 2027, or soon after needed approvals.

AR-2026F-SR13.s: The Senate adopted a resolution recognizing April as Child Abuse Prevention Month in Arkansas. It also commends Court Appointed Special Advocate, or CASA, programs and says a copy of the resolution should be given to Arkansas CASA programs. The resolution encourages people to support efforts that help protect children and strengthen families.

AR-2026F-SR14.s: The Senate resolution would recognize and celebrate Nucor Day at the State Capitol on April 15, 2026. It would also have a copy sent to Nucor’s chief executive officer after adoption.

AR-2026F-SR15.s: This resolution would let a bill be introduced to raise Arkansas’s homestead property tax credit. The credit would reduce real property taxes on a home from $600 to $675 each year. The change would apply to assessment years beginning on or after January 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-SR16.s: This resolution would let a senator introduce a bill about the Arkansas Children’s Educational Freedom Account Program. The planned bill would change how much money students get each year, add test score rules for keeping the account, bar some private school students from getting an account, and add some reporting duties for service providers who work with homeschooled students. It would also change the annual testing rules for students in the program.

AR-2026F-SR17.s: This resolution recognizes the Barton High School Bears boys' basketball team as the 2026 Class 2A state champions. It says the team won the title game 89-44 and finished the season 34-5. A copy of the resolution would be given to Head Coach Chris Williams.

AR-2026F-SR18.s: The Senate resolution would recognize the Earle High School Bulldogs boys' basketball team as the 2025 and 2026 Class 1A state champions. It notes the team won both titles, with Ta'ron Hurst named the Most Valuable Player in both years. A copy of the resolution would be given to Head Coach Carl Miller after adoption.

AR-2026F-SR19.s: The Arkansas Senate resolution would recognize the Earle High School Lady Bulldogs girls' basketball team as the 2026 Class 1A state champions. It notes that the team won the title on March 12, 2026, and that a copy of the resolution would be given to Head Coach Steven Jefferson. The resolution also names the team members and coaches, and says Jada Maples was the most valuable player.

AR-2026F-SR2.s: Adopted by the Senate, this resolution allows the Arkansas House or Senate, or both, to take recesses of four straight days or more during the 2026 fiscal session. The House could do so by the Speaker’s order, and the Senate by the President Pro Tempore’s order.

AR-2026F-SR20.s: A Senate resolution would authorize the introduction of a bill to change the Industrial Development Authorities Expansion Act. The bill would change who can serve on an industrial development authority board, allow some board members to be removed for good cause, and say these authorities must follow local zoning and planning rules. It would also change rules for acquiring property and say the act takes effect right away if approved.

AR-2026F-SR21.s: This resolution authorized the filing of a bill to create the Arkansas Property Rights Protection From Sharia Law Act. The bill would set rules for some residential property deals run through business entities, including required disclosures, limits on dispute rules, and limits on fees or transfer blocks. It would also let the Attorney General enforce violations under the state deceptive trade laws.

AR-2026F-SR22.s: The Arkansas Senate resolution recognized and commended the Legacy Keepers Nurse Honor Guard of Arkansas for its service to nursing across the state. It also said a copy of the resolution would be given to the group’s leaders after adoption.

AR-2026F-SR23.s: The Senate would honor John Pendleton Reed for his service to the Senate and to Arkansas. It says he retired after more than 35 years with the Senate as public information officer. A copy of the resolution would be given to him by the Secretary of the Senate.

AR-2026F-SR24.s: This Senate resolution would honor Amelia Lisowe for her achievements, service, and representation of Arkansas as Miss Arkansas' Teen 2025. It also says a copy of the resolution would be given to her by the Secretary of the Senate. A resolution is a formal statement by lawmakers, not a law.

AR-2026F-SR25.s: This resolution would recognize the League of Women Voters of Arkansas for its work in civic engagement, voter education, and service to the state. It would also recognize League Day at the Capitol, an event where members observe the legislative process and meet with elected officials. The Senate would commend the group’s members and volunteers for encouraging people to take part in government.

AR-2026F-SR26.s: The Senate resolution would congratulate Justin Tate for being chosen as a Guardian of the Flame for the Special Olympics torch run. It says he will carry the Flame of Hope to the opening ceremonies of the 2026 Special Olympics USA Games.

AR-2026F-SR27.s: This resolution recognizes the Elkins High School Elks football team as the 2025 Class 4A state champions. It says the team won the title on December 13, 2025, by beating Dardanelle High School 31-14, and finished the season 14-1. A copy of the resolution would be given to Head Coach Zach Watson.

AR-2026F-SR28.s: The Senate resolution would proclaim April 21, 2026, as Arkansas Lineworker Appreciation Day at the State Capitol. It would also commend Arkansas utility lineworkers for keeping power on and helping protect public safety.

AR-2026F-SR29.s: The Senate resolution would recognize April 22, 2026, as Arkansas School for Mathematics, Sciences, and the Arts Day at the State Capitol. It would also congratulate students from the school for their science fair results and their trip to the Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair in Phoenix, Arizona, on May 9-15, 2026. The resolution names several students and their project awards and honors.

AR-2026F-SR30.s: The Senate adopted a resolution honoring Loy Bailey for his 48 years of service at the Arkansas Department of Health. It also thanks him for his work in his community and the state and wishes him well in retirement. A copy of the resolution would be given to him by the Secretary of the Senate.

AR-2026F-SR31.s: This Senate resolution recognizes Coach Van Compton for her 51-year coaching career and her impact on women’s volleyball and athletics in Arkansas. It also congratulates her on her retirement from the University of Arkansas at Little Rock and her induction into the Arkansas Sports Hall of Fame. The Senate adopted the resolution and directed that copies be given to her, the university’s athletics department, and the Little Rock Juniors Volleyball Club.

AR-2026F-SR32.s: The Senate resolution would recognize the Parkview Arts and Sciences Magnet High School Patriots boys' basketball team as the 2026 Class 5A state champions. It also says a copy of the resolution would be given to Head Coach Jason Harrison after adoption.

AR-2026F-SR33.s: This resolution recognizes the Van Buren High School Pointers wrestling team as the 2025-2026 Class 5A state champions and the Lady Pointers as the 2025-2026 Class 5A state runners-up. It also notes the teams’ tournament results and says copies of the resolution would be given to the coaches.

AR-2026F-SR34.s: The Arkansas Senate resolution would recognize the Arkansas Tech University Golden Suns women’s cross country team for winning the Great American Conference Championship. It also says a copy of the resolution would be given to Head Coach Gabe Sams after adoption. The team members and coaches are named in the resolution, along with several honors earned by team members and the coach.

AR-2026F-SR35.s: The Arkansas Senate resolution honors Coach Dave Wilbers for his years leading the Arkansas Tech University women’s Golden Suns basketball team and congratulates him on his retirement. It says he had many wins and team titles during his 19 seasons as head coach. After adoption, a copy of the resolution would be given to him by the Secretary of the Senate.

AR-2026F-SR36.s: The Senate resolution would honor Miss Arkansas 2025 Kennedy Holland for her achievements and service. It also says a copy of the resolution would be given to her by the Secretary of the Senate. The measure affects Kennedy Holland.

AR-2026F-SR37.s: This resolution would bar Arkansas Girls State from using the Senate chamber for its 2026 meeting and would also block access to the Bureau of Legislative Research’s bill drafting help during that meeting. It would be lifted if the Senate’s president pro tempore finds that the American Legion Auxiliary has let certain students, who were denied because of missed deadlines, take part in the 2026 meeting. The resolution also urges the American Legion Auxiliary to rethink any decision that would keep those students from participating.

AR-2026F-SR38.s: The Senate resolution would recognize Kopper Kettle Candies for its candy-making work and its national ranking as the top candy store in Arkansas and the fifth-best in the United States. It would also direct that a copy of the resolution be given to Thomas Greer after adoption.

AR-2026F-SR39.s: The Senate adopted a resolution to honor Arkansas public servants and to observe Public Service Recognition Week from May 3 through May 9, 2026. It recognizes the work of state, local, and federal public workers in areas like teaching, health, elections, safety, and infrastructure. The resolution also calls on people in Arkansas to acknowledge their service.

AR-2026F-SR4.s: This resolution would allow a bill to be introduced that would change Arkansas’s revenue stabilization law, create funds, and move money to and from funds and fund accounts. The bill text says it would take effect on July 1, 2026, under an emergency clause.

AR-2026F-SR40.s: The Senate resolution would recognize four 2025 winners of the IBLA Grand Prize International Music Competition and welcome them to Arkansas. It would also commend the competition and festival for musical performances, education programs, and cultural exchange in Arkansas. The resolution was adopted.

AR-2026F-SR5.s: This resolution authorizes a bill to change Arkansas’s Revenue Stabilization Law, create funds, and move money to and from funds and fund accounts. The proposed bill would also declare an emergency and take effect on July 1, 2026. The Senate adopted the resolution.

AR-2026F-SR6.s: This resolution would let a bill be introduced to create the Equal Distribution County Turnback Fund and give counties extra money from certain state tax revenue. Each fiscal year, once the fund reaches $150 million, the state would send $2 million to each county, with most of that money for roads, water and sewer work, and county equipment. The rest would support fire, law enforcement, or other county community projects. It also says the act would take effect on July 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-SR7.s: This resolution would let a senator introduce a bill to change Arkansas rules for digital asset mining businesses and businesses that use blockchain networks. It would also change what local governments can do about home digital asset mining and other mining businesses, including some limits on local rules, permits, zoning, and utility rates.

AR-2026F-SR8.s: The resolution would have let lawmakers introduce a bill to charge digital asset mining businesses fees for extra electrical power use and add oversight rules. It would affect mining businesses already running and new ones that start after the law’s effective date. The money would go to state agencies for monitoring and enforcement work.

AR-2026F-SR9.s: This resolution would let a senator introduce a bill that would ban digital asset mining businesses and home miners from using computers made or assembled by a covered foreign entity, or software developed by one. A covered foreign entity includes certain people or groups tied to China or Russia, or listed on federal screening lists. The bill would also set criminal penalties for violations.

AR-2026S1-HB1001.s: This act lowers Arkansas income tax rates for individuals, trusts, and estates for tax years starting on or after January 1, 2026. It also sets new corporate income tax rates for Arkansas and foreign corporations for tax years starting on or after January 1, 2027, with rates of 1%, 2%, 3%, and 4.1% based on income levels.

AR-2026S1-SB1.s: The law lowers Arkansas income tax rates for individuals, trusts, estates, and corporations. For tax years starting on or after January 1, 2026, it sets new individual tax brackets, and for tax years starting on or after January 1, 2027, it lowers the corporate income tax rate. It became Act 2 on May 6, 2026.
